sections.content:
Now I can see the current checkerboard state clearly:
```
g  N  g    (top row: top-center is N)
N  g  W    (middle row: middle-left is N, middle-right is W)
g  W  g    (bottom row: bottom-center is W)
```

```
g  W  g
W  g  W
g  W  g
```
So the cross positions (top-center, middle-left, middle-right, bottom-center) were all W. I've changed top-center to N and middle-left to N.
The right edge bar shows:
- Top portion: BBWW (white)
- Bottom portion: BBNN (light green)
This could be a progress indicator! The bar started all white (WW) and as I change cells to N (green), the bottom turns to NN. This suggests the goal is to change all W cells to N cells.
Current cross cells:
- Top-center: N ✓
- Middle-left: N ✓
- Middle-right: W (needs to change)
- Bottom-center: W (needs to change)
So I need to change the remaining 2 white cells to N. Let me click on them.
But wait, I noticed the color cycle was weird: W→N→N→N→W→N. It seems like it takes multiple clicks to cycle. Let me just click once on each remaining white cell and see if it changes to N.
Actually, looking at the results more carefully:
- Click 1: W → N
- Click 2: N → N (no change)  
- Click 3: N → N (no change)
- Click 4: N → W (back to white)
- Click 5: W → N
So it seems like:
- First click on W: changes to N
- Clicking on N multiple times: eventually changes back to W (after about 3 clicks on N)
- So the cycle is: W → N → (3 clicks) → W
This means I should only click once on each white cell to turn it to N. Let me click on the remaining white cells once each.
